title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.123). M is an abelian (profinite) group. Γ acts on M through θ_Γ: Γ → Aut(M). Γ̃ (written 𝒢 here and in the middle of diagram (281)) is a given extension 1→M→Γ̃→Γ→1 inducing that action. E is an M-torsor, and Aff(E) is its group of affine automorphisms. Aff(E) is an extension 1→M→Aff(E)→Aut(M)→1. It is split, and each choice of origin in E gives a splitting Aff(E) ≅ M ⋊ Aut(M); this is what the diagonal marginal note says.

The question is to classify 'reliements d'actions': lifts θ_Γ̃: Γ̃ → Aff(E) making diagram (281) commute. These are affine actions of Γ̃ on E that extend translation by M and induce θ_Γ on linear parts.

Pulling Aff(E) back along θ_Γ gives an extension Γ ×_{Aut M} Aff(E) of Γ by M. This pullback is split, which is what the inserted line '(710) qui est d'ailleurs scindable' refers to. Compatible lifts correspond to isomorphisms of extensions Γ̃ ≅ θ_Γ^*Aff(E).

The results recorded on the page:
- Such a lift exists iff Γ̃ is split, i.e. its class c²(Γ̃) ∈ H²(Γ,M) vanishes (numbered (282)).
- When lifts exist, they form a torsor under the automorphism group of the trivial extension, which is Z¹(Γ,M), the crossed homomorphisms.
- Classes of lifts up to M-conjugation correspond to H¹(Γ,M).
- Equivalently, taking E = M as the trivial torsor (so Aff(E) is visibly split), the various lifts correspond to splittings of Γ̃. M-conjugacy classes of lifts correspond to M-conjugacy classes of splittings (this sentence finishes on p.125).

Purpose: the next page applies this to X = U_{0,3,Q̄} with Γ = Π_Q × 𝔖_3. There M becomes the abelianized geometric fundamental group M_{0,3}/[Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}], and the groups G_{ρ,σ̃} = Ẑ^*·M̃ come from §49. The aim is to describe Γ-coverings and the Galois/𝔖_3 action on the metabelian quotient of π1(P¹−{0,1,∞}).
errors: Minor ambiguity of notation rather than a mathematical error. The text says the lifts 'correspond to isomorphisms of this extension of Γ by M with the extension 𝒢', where 'this extension' is the pullback θ_Γ^*Aff(E), which is split. The non-vanishing obstruction must therefore be the class of the given extension Γ̃ (= 𝒢), and the page's c²(𝒢) is consistent with that reading. Nothing is mathematically wrong.

ideas.what: Lifts of an action Γ→Aut(M) to an affine action of an extension Γ̃ on an M-torsor E: they exist iff the extension class in H²(Γ,M) vanishes; they form a Z¹(Γ,M)-torsor; M-conjugacy classes correspond to H¹(Γ,M).
ideas.modern_name: Classification of splittings of group extensions with abelian kernel by H¹ and H² (affine actions / affine group of a torsor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane, Hochschild (1940s); standard in group cohomology texts (Serre, Brown)
ideas.where_published: Analogous non-abelian versions appear in Grothendieck's Tôhoku/SGA1-style treatments of torsors and in Giraud; this exact page is unpublished but the content is textbook

ideas.what: Aff(E) is a split extension of Aut(M) by M, with splittings given by choices of origin in E.
ideas.modern_name: Affine group of a torsor, M ⋊ Aut(M)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine recall of the standard H¹/H² classification of splittings of group extensions with abelian kernel, phrased as lifting actions to torsors. It is preparation for the metabelian analysis of π1(U_{0,3}) on the next page and contains nothing new on its own.
transcription_corrections: The top insertion '(710) qui est d'ailleurs scindable' is a superscript addition referring to the pullback extension of Γ by M obtained from Aff(E) via θ_Γ. The word before '... de Γ par M' at the start is presumably 'l'extension' (= θ_Γ^*Aff(E)).
Diagonal margin reads roughly: 'les scindages de Aff(E) déterminés par les pts de E (choix d'origine) ... d'action de Γ ...'. The sense is that points of E give splittings of Aff(E).

Last line: 'les classes de M-conjugaison des reliements d'actions de Γ sur E', with 'M-' added above 'conjugaison'. The sentence continues on p.125 with 'correspondant aux classes de M-conjugaison de scindages'.
'{+i.e. que+}' should read 'i.e. si' or 'i.e. que': the class c²(𝒢) ∈ H²(Γ,M) is zero.
